summary.oneLiner: Ramky Infrastructure Limited has received a credit rating upgrade from IVR BBB- to IVR BBB with a stable outlook, indicating a moderate degree of safety regarding timely servicing of financial obligations. The company's operational and financial performance for FY25 and 9M-FY26 have been taken into account. The upgrade reflects the company's improved credit profile, with a total bank facility of Rs. 706.47 crores. The company's focus on sustainable infrastructure and green buildings is expected to drive growth in the future.

financial scorecard / credit view: Credit Rating: IVR BBB with stable outlook by Infomerics Valuation and Rating Limited; Previous Rating: IVR BBB- with stable outlook
guidance / outlook: The company's outlook is stable, with a focus on executing projects and improving financial performance. The credit rating upgrade is expected to improve the company's access to funding and reduce borrowing costs.
segment / subsidiary detail: The company's construction and engineering segments are expected to drive growth, with a focus on sustainable infrastructure and green buildings.
growth verticals / optionality: The company's growth optionality is expected to come from its focus on sustainable infrastructure and green buildings, as well as its ability to execute projects efficiently.
capital allocation: The company's capital allocation is expected to focus on funding projects and improving financial performance.
risks & watch-items: The company's risks include execution risks, funding risks, and regulatory risks. The credit rating upgrade reduces the company's funding risks, but execution risks and regulatory risks remain.
non-obvious takeaways: The company's focus on sustainable infrastructure and green buildings is expected to drive growth in the future, and the credit rating upgrade is expected to improve the company's access to funding and reduce borrowing costs.

themes.title: Infrastructure EPC & roads order-book conversion
themes.need: India's record capital-outlay cycle (roads, metro, marine, hydro, tunnelling) gives diversified EPC contractors multi-year visibility - AFCONS tracks a ~INR4 lakh cr pipeline (70% domestic) and targets ~INR30,000cr FY27 inflow; NCC/DBL/PNCINFRA/GRINFRA/ASHOKA/CEIGALL carry large road/HAM books; AFCONS/PATELENG/AHLUCONT/PSPPROJECT add marine, hydro and building EPC. The binding issue is execution + client-payment cycles, not order intake.
themes.driver: L1-to-firm-order conversion (AFCONS Croatia/Vadhavan, DMRC awards); NHAI/HAM award pickup; monsoon-end execution ramp.
